Description: explicit — TileJSON url vs hand-wired tiles template
prompt: In a MapLibre vector source, should I use the `url` field pointing at a TileJSON endpoint, or just put the {z}/{x}/{y} template straight into the `tiles` array? My tile server offers both.
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### TL;DR  
**If the server gives you a TileJSON endpoint, point `url` at it.**  
Only fall back to a hand‑written `tiles` array when a TileJSON document does **not** exist (or you deliberately need to override something that TileJSON supplies).

---

## Why `url` is usually the right choice

| What you get automatically when you use `url` | What you have to do yourself when you use `tiles` |
|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **Tile URL template** – MapLibre reads it from the TileJSON. | You must write the `{z}/{x}/{y}` template yourself. |
| **Zoom range** (`minzoom` / `maxzoom`) – taken from the TileJSON. | If you omit them MapLibre assumes `maxzoom: 22`.  Requests for zooms the tileset doesn’t have will return empty tiles, often showing as “nothing draws” when you zoom in. |
| **Bounds / extent** – used for `fitBounds`, `maxBounds`, etc. | You have to supply them manually (or ignore them). |
| **Attribution** – pulled from TileJSON and shown in the UI. | You must add it yourself if you care about it. |
| **`vector_layers` list** – the authoritative list of source‑layer names and their attribute fields. | You have to look up the schema elsewhere (provider docs, your own generation script) and copy it into your style. |
| **Future‑proofing** – if the provider adds new layers or changes zoom limits, the TileJSON will reflect that without you touching the style. | You would have to edit the source definition again. |

Because all of those pieces are *metadata* that the style needs but that don’t affect the actual tile‑fetching code, letting MapLibre read them from a TileJSON keeps your source definition tiny and less error‑prone.

```json
{
  "type": "vector",
  "url": "https://tiles.example.com/tileset.json"
}
```

When the URL resolves to a valid TileJSON, MapLibre will:

1. Pull the `tiles` array (the real URL template) from the document.
2. Record `minzoom`, `maxzoom`, `bounds`, `attribution`, and the `vector_layers` array.
3. Expose those `source-layer` names for you to reference in style layers.

---

## When you *must* use `tiles`

| Situation | Reason |
|-----------|--------|
| The server only returns a raw tile URL template (e.g., `https://tiles.example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`). | No TileJSON exists, so there is nothing for `url` to fetch. |
| You need to **override** a value that the TileJSON provides (e.g., you want a different `maxzoom` than the one advertised). | You can still use `url` **and** add the overriding fields, but if you need to replace the whole TileJSON you can just write `tiles`. |
| You are serving **raster** tiles (or any non‑vector format) that don’t have a TileJSON endpoint. | Raster sources also support `tiles`, but they don’t have a `vector_layers` list, so the only thing you can supply is the template and optional metadata. |
| You are experimenting locally with a static set of tiles and don’t want to spin up a TileJSON server. | A quick `tiles` array is the fastest way to get something on the map. |

In those cases you must remember to add the missing metadata yourself:

```json
{
  "type": "vector",
  "tiles": ["https://tiles.example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf"],
  "minzoom": 0,
  "maxzoom": 14,
  "attribution": "© Example Tiles",
  "bounds": [-180, -85, 180, 85]
}
```

*If you forget `minzoom`/`maxzoom`, MapLibre will request zoom levels that don’t exist (up to 22) and you’ll see blank tiles at higher zooms.*

---

## Quick checklist before you decide

1. **Is there a TileJSON URL?**  
   - `GET https://tiles.example.com/tileset.json` → returns a JSON with `tiles`, `vector_layers`, etc. → **use `url`.**
2. **Does the TileJSON include `vector_layers`?**  
   - If yes, you can copy the exact `source-layer` names from there.  
   - If it’s missing, you’ll still get the tile URL and zoom range, but you’ll need to look up the schema elsewhere (provider docs, your own generation script).  
3. **Do you need to override any metadata?**  
   - You can still use `url` and add `minzoom`, `maxzoom`, `attribution`, etc. on top of it.  
   - Only use `tiles` when you have no TileJSON at all.  
4. **CORS & authentication**  
   - Both `url` and `tiles` are fetched via XHR/fetch, so the same CORS rules apply.  
   - If you need to add an `access_token` query param, you can either embed it in the TileJSON `tiles` entries (if you control the TileJSON) or add it to the `tiles` array yourself.  

---

## Example: Switching from `tiles` to `url`

You might start with a quick test like this:

```json
{
  "type": "vector",
  "tiles": ["https://tiles.example.com/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf"]
}
```

If you later discover that `https://tiles.example.com/tileset.json` exists, replace the source definition with:

```json
{
  "type": "vector",
  "url": "https://tiles.example.com/tileset.json"
}
```

*You can keep any extra fields you added (e.g., `promoteId`, `maxzoom`) – they will merge with the values from the TileJSON, with your explicit fields taking precedence.*

---

## TL;DR Recap

| Use `url` when | Use `tiles` when |
|----------------|------------------|
| A TileJSON endpoint is available (most hosted providers, Martin, TileServer‑GL, PMTiles, etc.). | No TileJSON exists (raw raster tiles, simple static vector tiles, or you’re prototyping). |
| You want MapLibre to auto‑populate zoom range, bounds, attribution, and source‑layer list. | You must manually supply those pieces yourself. |
| You want the source to stay in sync with any future changes the provider makes to the TileJSON. | You need full control over every field (rare). |

Following this rule eliminates the most common “nothing draws” bugs caused by missing zoom ranges or mismatched `source-layer` names, and it keeps your style definition clean and maintainable. Happy mapping!
